question: I own a 2,500 sqm plot here. How much of the land am I allowed to cover with building?
expected_answer_short: Up to 40% of the plot, with relaxations possible from the TOD Committee.
notes: Only the location step can know this is a TOD plot rather than ordinary housing.

question: What is the most floor space I could put up on a site at this spot?
expected_answer_short: Base 400, rising to a maximum of 500 once extra charges are paid.

question: My piece of land measures about 1,500 sqm. Is that big enough to join the scheme that covers this address?
expected_answer_short: No: the minimum is 2,000 sqm.

question: Am I obliged to sign up to the development scheme covering this land, or may I stay on my old approvals?
expected_answer_short: Taking part is voluntary; existing approvals continue if you do not.

question: How many car spaces would I have to provide for a building at this location?
expected_answer_short: One equivalent car space for every 100 sqm of floor area.

question: If I build flats here, how much of the building has to be homes rather than shops or offices?
expected_answer_short: At least 65% of the permitted floor area has to be residential.

question: How long should the authority take to clear a building proposal for a site like this?
expected_answer_short: Up to 60 days from a complete submission.

question: How far back from the big new highway do the special building rules reach at this spot?
expected_answer_short: A 250 m band measured from the edge of the road's right of way.

question: What width of road does my plot need to front onto before I can build under the rules here?
expected_answer_short: A road with a right of way of at least 18 m.

question: Can my brother and I put our two adjoining plots together to build one project at this address?
expected_answer_short: Yes, plots may be amalgamated and reconstituted under the corridor policy.

question: Is affordable housing something I must include in a project at this location?
expected_answer_short: Yes, it is a requirement of the corridor policy.

question: Only part of my land falls inside the area with the better building rules. Does it still count?
expected_answer_short: Yes, if at least 75% of the plot lies inside the zone.

question: Once my farmland here is built up, how much floor space will each plot be allowed?
expected_answer_short: An FAR of 200 on each plot in the scheme.

question: If I hand over my land here for development, what proportion do I get back?
expected_answer_short: Landowners keep up to 60%, with at least 40% going to DDA.

question: How much land would a group of us need to gather before we can start a scheme here?
expected_answer_short: At least 20 hectares of contiguous land.

question: My plot here sits inside the old village settlement. Do these rules reach it?
expected_answer_short: No: Lal Dora and extended Lal Dora land is left out.

question: Who is responsible for putting in the roads and parks when my land here gets developed?
expected_answer_short: DDA acts as the main anchor for roads, parks and services.

question: Can I put up a house on this piece of land?
expected_answer_short: No: on the active floodplain nothing may be built, and only recreational use is allowed.
notes: The hardest location question: nothing in the wording hints at the river.

question: Someone has thrown up a wall and a shed on the land next to mine here. Who has to act?
expected_answer_short: The Vice Chairman of DDA was directed by the High Court to clear encroachments.

question: Is a petrol pump something that could be allowed at this spot?
expected_answer_short: No: fuel stations are allowed in all use zones except recreational ones and Zone O.

question: What, if anything, is this land allowed to be used for?
expected_answer_short: Recreational use only on the active floodplain, with limited public uses by permission.

question: I have a 250 sqm plot here and want to rebuild my house. How much can I cover and how high?
expected_answer_short: Plotted housing norms in chapter 7 set coverage, FAR and dwelling units by plot size.
notes: Checks the opposite case: no policy zone, so the general norms should win.

question: What is the smallest site I would need here to build a block of flats?
expected_answer_short: 3,000 sqm for group housing, on a road of at least 18 m right of way.

question: My building here is forty years old. What is the least land I need to redevelop the whole thing?
expected_answer_short: 3,000 sqm for residential, 1,000 sqm for commercial, industrial and PSP.

question: Could I run a small workshop out of my home at this address?
expected_answer_short: Household industries from the annexure lists are allowed in residential premises.

question: Does the 2047 plan take over from the 2021 one?
expected_answer_short: Yes, but plans approved earlier stay approved.

question: From what date is the new master plan in force?
expected_answer_short: From the date it was notified in the official gazette, 20 August 2026.

question: How wide is the band along a metro line where the transit development rules apply?
expected_answer_short: 500 m either side of the centre line, plus a 500 m radius around major stations.

question: What is the smallest plot that can be developed under the transit oriented policy?
Where does the transit oriented development policy not apply?
expected_answer_short: Zone O and buffers, low density areas, monument prohibited areas and other sensitive areas.

question: Which road is the high density corridor built along?
expected_answer_short: Urban Extension Road II.

question: What floor area ratio can a residential project get in the high density corridor?
expected_answer_short: The FAQ gives the permissible FAR by use for HDC plots.

question: Which planning zones does the land pooling policy cover?
expected_answer_short: K-I, L, N, P-II, part of J and part of P-I.

question: What charges does a landowner pay under land pooling?
expected_answer_short: Development charges, plus other applicable charges.

question: May anything at all be built on the active floodplain of the river?
expected_answer_short: No construction; recreational use only, with limited public uses by permission.

question: Which planning zone covers the river and its banks?
expected_answer_short: Zone O, named River Yamuna / Riverfront.

question: What did the High Court tell DDA to do about illegal building on the river bank?
expected_answer_short: The Vice Chairman was made nodal officer and told to remove all encroachments.

question: Who was appointed to coordinate the agencies on the Yamuna encroachment case?
expected_answer_short: The Vice Chairman of DDA, as nodal officer.

question: What is the smallest plot that can be redeveloped in a commercial area?
expected_answer_short: 1,000 sqm for commercial, industrial and PSP; 3,000 sqm for residential.

question: By how much can the floor area ratio go up when an area is regenerated?
expected_answer_short: Up to 1.5 times the base FAR.

question: Is rebuilding allowed on a plotted residential property?
expected_answer_short: Only reconstruction at the permitted FAR; redevelopment is not allowed.

question: What is the permitted floor area ratio and smallest plot for a group housing scheme?
expected_answer_short: FAR 200 and 3,000 sqm, or 2,000 sqm in Lal Dora, on an 18 m road.

question: What is a studio apartment under this plan?
expected_answer_short: A residential unit with a carpet area of 40 to 60 sqm.

question: How big does a local shopping centre site have to be?
expected_answer_short: 3,000 sqm with an 18 m right of way; a convenience centre needs 1,000 sqm.

question: Can a hotel be built on a commercial plot, and what are its limits?
expected_answer_short: Yes; chapter 8 sets hotel coverage, FAR and height.

question: Can an industrial plot be switched to commercial use?
expected_answer_short: Yes, use conversion to commercial and PSP use is possible on conditions.

question: Is extra floor space available for housing factory workers?
expected_answer_short: Yes: plots of 5,000 sqm and above can take an extra 15% FAR for worker housing.

question: Where do I look up which activities are allowed on a particular kind of premise?
expected_answer_short: Annexures 18 to 22 of the plan list permitted use premises and activities.

question: What rules govern a petrol pump: plot size, coverage and road width?
expected_answer_short: At least a 24 m road, 20% coverage, FAR 40, and a plot of at least 30 m by 36 m.

question: How many planning zones is Delhi divided into?
expected_answer_short: 17, lettered A to P with no zone I.

question: How much property tax will I owe on a flat in Rohini?
expected_answer_short: Not in the corpus: property tax is a municipal matter, not the master plan.

question: What is the permitted floor space index in Mumbai?
expected_answer_short: Not in the corpus: these documents cover Delhi only.

question: Can my landlord raise my rent this year?
expected_answer_short: Not in the corpus: rent control is separate legislation.

question: What can I build on my plot here?
expected_answer_short: The point is outside Delhi, so this plan does not apply to it.
notes: Point outside Delhi; should abstain with reason outside_delhi before any LLM call.

question: How much would a 200 sqm plot here sell for?
expected_answer_short: Not in the corpus: the plan sets rules, not prices.
notes: Inside Delhi but the documents do not settle it.

question: Which bank will give me a loan to build on this land?
expected_answer_short: Not in the corpus: nothing in these documents is about finance.

question: How long will the authority actually take to answer my file in practice?
expected_answer_short: Not settled: the plan gives a 60 day limit but says nothing about real waiting times.
notes: A stated limit exists but the question asks about practice, which the documents do not cover.

question: Will my building plan be approved?
expected_answer_short: Not answerable: no document can say whether a particular application will succeed.

question: What are the rules for building in Gurugram just across the border?
expected_answer_short: Not in the corpus: Gurugram is in Haryana and outside this plan.

question: Who won the court case about the Yamuna floodplain in the end?
expected_answer_short: Not settled: the order gives directions and disposes of the petition, it names no winner.
notes: Adjacent to the corpus but the documents do not answer it.
